This turn resolved the central question of the audit — whether the supplied implementation has been mutated.

The Go module cache contains a **sum.golang.org-signed** record for `github.com/hashicorp/raft v1.7.3` (`h1:DxpEqZJysHN0wK+fviai5mFcSYsCkNpFUl1xpAW8Rbo=`, with a valid `— sum.golang.org ...` note), and `GOPROXY=off go mod download -json github.com/hashicorp/raft@v1.7.3` reports that same `Sum` along with `Origin.Hash = c0dc6a0b...` / `Ref = refs/tags/v1.7.3`. Since the audited `work/`/`source/` tree is byte-for-byte identical to that verified zip (checked by `md5sum` and recursive `diff` earlier), the implementation under audit is the **unmodified upstream v1.7.3 release** — no source-level mutation exists in the audited scope. The signature cannot be forged offline, so this also removes the "cache seeded from a mutated tree" ambiguity I flagged last turn.

Supporting results: `go build ./...` succeeds, `go vet ./...` is clean, and `go test -short ./...` fails only in socket-opening tests (all `operation not permitted`; TCP is blocked in this sandbox, no `isolated_exec` helper available).

Source coverage this turn: `configurationChangeChIfStable`, `log.go`/LogStore & MonotonicLogStore contracts, `log_cache.go`, `future.go` (`deferError` respond-once), and `api.go` `BootstrapCluster`/`RecoverCluster`, all consistent with upstream. Combined with the earlier review of the commit/vote/prevote/replication/snapshot/FSM paths, no contradiction with Raft semantics was found.

Net: **no concrete correctness defect identified in this baseline**, and I have not fabricated one. Remaining open work is recorded in the report (a `-race` run of the in-memory subset, and line-by-line review of the remaining transport/snapshot-store files); the tree is otherwise fully accounted for as pristine upstream v1.7.3.
